claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while GPS placed him 351 m from the pickup point, so the arrival condition of NS-1(ii) fails outright: he was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data.
The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point at any time — his closest approach was 319 m at 08:46:50 — and the platform itself never recorded him arriving (driver_arrived_at is null).

After the tap the driver spent 0 seconds inside the 200 m pickup radius; the 4 minutes he was stationary (08:47:00–08:51:00) were at 350 m from the pickup point, so the continuous-wait requirement of NS-1(iii) is not met.
Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) do not all hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not collectable and must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The driver pressed the arrival button while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius (351 m > 200 m), which is the abuse-of-the-arrival-button situation for which NS-2 attaches a flag_account request against the driver.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by GPS (stationary only at 350 m from the pickup point) and by the chat, where the rider said at 08:48 that she was at the pickup point and saw no car while the driver had already claimed at 08:47 to be there; the system records prevail.

The chat record is complete (3 messages, all timestamped) and the timeline covers the whole booking from acceptance 08:44:00 to the driver's cancellation 08:51:00, so there is no G12 evidence gap that would push the case to manual review instead of a refund.
The rider has never had a no-show or route dispute upheld (0 upheld in 90 days), so there is no pattern on the rider's side that could support the driver's no-show claim.

weaknesses: The driver did accept and did wait around for roughly 4 minutes (F2, F3) and did send a plausible arrival message (F8), so the driver can argue he made a genuine attempt to collect the rider even if he was not at the pickup point.

The rider's own 08:48 message (F9) proves only that she was at the pickup point and saw no car; it does not show the exact spot she stood in, and she never sent a message challenging the driver's "I'm Here" claim before the cancellation at 08:51:00 (F10).
The rider has 1 dispute in 90 days, not upheld (F16), so a judge inclined to weigh profile history mildly may note some prior disputation on her side, though it is not a finding against her.

claims.assertion: The system records show the driver did not satisfy the arrival precondition: he tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 while 351 m from the pickup point and spent 0 s within 200 m after the tap (F5), and his closest approach in the whole trip was 319 m at 08:46:50 (F1).

The stationarity the driver relies on was at 350 m from the pickup point, not at the pickup point: he was stationary 08:47:00–08:51:00 at (1.4069, 103.8988), which is 350 m from the pickup (F2), so the 4 min 0 s wait does not satisfy the "at the pick-up location" limb of NS-1(ii).

The platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point — driver_arrived_at is null (F4), and the driver's own message at 08:47 says only "Reached already … come out please" (F8) without stating any location, so there is no record of his whereabouts at the pickup point.

The rider's single message at 08:48 reports she was at the pickup point and saw no car (F9), which is consistent with the GPS evidence that the driver was about 320–350 m away, so nothing in the chat places the driver at the pickup location.

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" (F12) is a statement alone and is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records F1, F2 and F5, so the system records control and the statement cannot establish NS-1(ii) or NS-1(iii).
The cancellation fee of $6.61 is on record (F6, F3); because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not met, the whole sum is refundable to the rider and the correct outcome for this case is refund_full of $6.61.

No host-side ground excuses the 350 m standoff: no speed-band records (F13) and no traffic incidents (F14) near the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15), so the driver's position is unexplained by any traffic fact.

The chat record is complete — three messages, every one timestamped (F11) — so the G12 incompleteness route to a manual referral does not apply and the case can be decided on the records: nothing in the exchange (F8, F9, F10) shows the rider at a wrong place or refusing to board.

Tapping "I'm Here" while 351 m outside the pickup point is the exact conduct NS-2 identifies for an account flag, so the ruling should carry flag_account in addition to refund_full; the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over 992 trips (F17) and the rider has filed 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F16), but profiles cannot be used to decide the fee itself.

weaknesses: F2 shows the driver was genuinely stationary for a full 4 min 0 s and at 08:47 he messaged that he had "reached already" with the car description (F8); on a fair reading he was waiting somewhere near the area, and a person unfamiliar with the pickup point may believe 350 m is "at" the mall. This is the strongest point for the driver, but it still fails NS-1(ii) because F5 records 351 m at the tap and 0 s within 200 m after it.

The driver cancelled 7 min 0 s after acceptance (F3) and had waited 4 min 0 s (F2), so he cleared the "more than 3 minutes" duration limb of NS-1(iii) on its face; the rider's side of the weakness is that the only duration failure is the location limb, not the waiting time.

The rider's own message at 08:48 (F9) does not state exactly where she was standing, so the record does not affirmatively prove she was at the designated pickup point either; the driver's side can argue the meeting point was simply not matched — but F4 (driver_arrived_at null) and F1 (never within 200 m) still leave NS-1(ii) unsatisfied.

F17 shows a long-tenure driver (1346 d, 4.85 rating, 0 upheld disputes in 90 d), which the driver's side will use to argue this was a one-off location error rather than fee abuse; this can mitigate the flag_account request, though it cannot cure the NS-1 failure.

Conceded: no speed bands (F13), no incidents (F14) and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F15) leave the driver's 350 m standoff unexplained by any traffic fact, and none of these facts places him at the pickup point.

Conceded: the chat record is complete with three timestamped messages (F11) and the timeline runs from acceptance 08:44:00 to cancellation 08:51:00 (F3, F4), so no G12 gap exists and the case can be decided on the records as my C7 argued.

Conceded that the flag is warranted on the conduct itself, per my C5: the tap at 351 m (F5) is the NS-2 arrival-button abuse the fee rule attaches a flag to; the driver's clean 90-day record over 992 trips (F17) may inform how Ryde weighs the flag but does not cure the NS-1 failure, and profiles (F16, F17) cannot decide the fee.
Conceded on the law and the record: F5 places the tap 351 m from the pickup point and F1 shows he never came within 200 m, so NS-1(ii) is not satisfied and I do not contest it.
Conceded; F1 (closest approach 319 m at 08:46:50) and F4 (driver_arrived_at null) are system records and neither can be argued away, so NS-1(i)/(ii) stand unmet.

Conceded; F2 shows the 4 min 0 s stationary period at 350 m and F5 shows 0 s inside 200 m after the tap, so the continuous-wait limb of NS-1(iii) fails on the location requirement even though the duration on its face exceeded 3 minutes.
Conceded; with NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) unmet the $6.61 on record (F3, F6) is not collectable and NS-2 requires refund_full, which is the outcome I already requested.

Conceded as to the flag: F5 shows the arrival button pressed 351 m outside the pickup radius, which is precisely the conduct NS-2 attaches flag_account to, and my client's clean record (F17: 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days over 992 trips) is a mitigating profile fact that cannot displace the flag but is the only reason to keep it a review and not a finding of fraud.

Conceded; F12 is a post-hoc driver statement and the system records (F2 stationary at 350 m, F1 never inside 200 m, F9 rider at the pickup point seeing no car) prevail over it under the priority of gps/timeline over statements.

Conceded; F11 (3 messages, all timestamped) and F3 (acceptance 08:44:00 to cancellation 08:51:00) mean there is no G12 evidence gap, so the case is decided on the records rather than referred for incompleteness.

Not contested on the fee: F16 shows 0 upheld no-show disputes on the rider's side, but profile facts may not decide a case, so the refund rests on F5 and F1 unmet against NS-1(ii), not on either party's history.

I do not withdraw D9, but I narrow it: the flag_account follows from F5 alone under NS-2, and I ask the judge to record F17 (long tenure, 4.85 rating, 0 upheld) as the context that this was a location error, not fee abuse.
